What Davie Fogarty's video gets right, and what we take from it

“If I Wanted to Hit $1M/Month in Ecommerce, I'd Do This,” Davie Fogarty Mentors, 8:44, premiered Nov 15, 2026. Based on the full transcript and your 4 screenshots.

The verdict

Where we're aheadHis video starts after you already have a product, a supplier and sales. We did those parts properly:
  • Product chosen from real sales data
  • Costs and break-even worked out before buying
  • Suppliers found and ranked
Where he's aheadThese are the levers that turn visitors into buyers. We haven't built them yet:
  • A heavy offer stack
  • A product page copied from the winners and tested
  • An AI ad machine: winning ads in, 3 options in his brand out, reviewed and launched weekly
  • A weekly ad-volume target
  • A daily profit tracker
The real hack

He doesn't ask Claude for one answer. He asks for 3 options, then corrects them with what he can actually deliver, then asks to see it as a page before deciding. That loop works for anything.

His 3 steps, decoded

STEP 1Fix the offer and product page
  • Copy what the top direct-to-consumer brands do (he uses Gruns)
  • Bundles, a pre-selected best deal, price per day or per serving, free shipping, a guarantee
  • Have Claude Code rebuild the page, 3 versions, then split-test
STEP 2Launch more ads, every week
  • Ads wear out in about 2 months now (his coaches' estimate)
  • Set a weekly target for new ads (20, then 30, then 40)
  • Name ads the same way every time, and track win rate
STEP 3Track profit every day
  • True landed cost per product, updated monthly
  • Two targets: MER (sales divided by ad spend) and the minimum MER to make your profit target
  • Look at it daily before touching ad budgets

Your screenshots, explained

These are the moments in the video where his prompts and results are readable. YouTube's preview frames only show him talking, so these are the prompts we have.

The ad machine he built (from your new screenshots)

This is the part the transcript only mentions in passing (“I've built our own AI ad machine”). Your screenshots show how it works: 6 stages, from studying winning ads to tracking profit.

1Collect the winners
2Turn each winner into a pattern, then 3 options
3Review and edit like a designer
4Launch on a weekly rhythm
5Measure it
6Watch profit, not revenue
A detail worth stealing: his project sidebar shows a file ending in product-bible.md and a saved skill called facebook-static-tool. A product bible is one document of true facts about the product (specs, claims you can prove, the offer, the brand voice) that every ad prompt reads, so the AI can't invent things. We should write ours before any ad is made.

Our version, with tools we already have connected

CollectForeplay is already connected. We pulled 23 competitor ads on Nov 15. Next: the top 10 longest-running ads each for RuffRover, Ruff Liners, 4Knines and 2 to 3 big pet brands.
PatternClaude labels each ad's pattern: problem question (“Does your dog slide around?”), before and after, comparison, founder story, reply to a comment, news card.
Generate3 options per pattern in our brand. Unlike his, ours must use photos and clips of our real sample (our rule), plus true facts from a product bible.
Review boardA page like his Creative OS: pick an option, type a change, download the PNG. This is squarely your software skill set, and I can build version 1.
LaunchThe Meta Ads connector is already connected. Claude uploads ads as PAUSED into this week's ad set, named product_type_date_creator. Nothing goes live without your yes.
MeasureWeekly: new ads vs target, win rate, and MER against our numbers (break-even 2.09, target 2.79 at scale; 3.81 and 5.08 during the test).

Prompt library: his prompts, rewritten for us

Left: his wording, from your screenshots or what he says in the video. Right: the version I'd use for our extender. Copy any of them into Claude.

Find the brands to copyHis step 1 (said in the video, not shown)
His prompt
Find the best direct-to-consumer brands in [niche], not the giants: brands doing serious sales mostly through their own site. List their product pages and what each one does on the page to make people buy.
Our version
Find the 5 best direct-to-consumer brands selling dog back-seat extenders or dog car gear (like RuffRover, Ruff Liners, 4Knines). For each, list every product page feature: offers, bundles, guarantees, free extras, reviews, icons, delivery promises. Rank the features by how often they appear.
Build the offer stackHis screenshot 2
His prompt
Can you please come up with the offer stack that you would recommend for the pre-workout, based on what a lot of the competitors are doing? Also, make sure that you consider the unique selling proposition: one being Hudson, and also the fact that we're trying to sell people to stop them from getting banned. Is there anything unique that we could add there? I definitely want quite a heavy offer with multiple things that they get when they purchase.
Our version
Come up with 3 offer stacks for our dog back-seat extender kit at about $149, based on what RuffRover, Ruff Liners and 4Knines do. Our unique angles: it fits your car or we pay the return, a 2-measurement fit check, and door guards that never touch the window. I want a heavy offer with several things included, but mostly extras that cost us little (guides, tools, warranty). Give each option's price tiers, what's free, and the guarantee.

A first offer stack for our extender (draft)

Following his method: 3 options for you to react to. Prices are placeholders until supplier quotes come back. Then the fee calculator checks each tier before anything goes live.

Option A · SimpleOne kit, everything included
  • Extender + 2 door guards + seat-belt tether, about $149
  • Free shipping
  • “Fits your car or we pay the return”
  • 1-year warranty, no registration
Option B · Recommended3 tiers, best one pre-selected
  • Kit only
  • Most popular: kit + bed topper (RuffRover's longest-running ads use a free bed)
  • Two-car pack: 2 kits at a discount
  • Free extras on every tier: printed fit card, road-trip checklist, fur-removal tool
Option C · Heavy stackHis style: lots of free extras
  • Kit + door guards (shown at their real separate price once we sell them separately) + tether + travel bowl + fur tool
  • Digital: road-trip planner and fit finder (your software edge)
  • Guarantee plus warranty
  • No sweepstakes or monthly prize draw (see below)

His profit target, with our numbers

MER = total sales divided by total ad spend. Below the break-even MER, ads lose money. The target adds our 25% safety cushion. Computed from our fee model for the own store with Meta ads at $149.

Test batch (air freight)5.08target MER · break-even 3.81
At scale (sea freight)2.79target MER · break-even 2.09

In plain words: during the test, every $1 of ads needs to bring in about $5 of sales. Once we buy in bulk by sea, about $2.80 is enough. That's why the big order matters.

Things to be careful with
  • It's a sales funnel too: the video ends in his paid mentorship. “Profitable from day one” is one client story, not proof.
  • Prize draws are risky: his “monthly draw” is a sweepstakes. Those have state rules, and large prizes can require registration in some states, Florida included. We skip it.
  • Strike-through prices must be real: a “was $149.85” price has to be one people actually paid. Ours will be (FTC rules on price comparisons and “free” offers).
  • Photos off the internet: fine for a private mockup only. Live pages use photos of our real sample.
  • 20 to 40 ads a week assumes a big budget. Our version: 3 to 5 new creator videos a week, tracked the same way.
